pairs: After these things, and after this manner of truth,
Sennacherib, the king of the Assyrians arrived.
And when Hezekiah had seen this,
et totum belli impetum verti contra Jerusalem,
and that the entire force of the war was turning against Jerusalem,
he took counsel with the rulers
and with the most valiant men,
ut obturarent capita fontium qui erant extra urbem:
so that they might obstruct the heads of the springs which were beyond the city.
And with everyone discerning the same judgment about this,
he gathered together a great multitude,
and they obstructed all the springs,
et rivum qui fluebat in medio terræ,
and the brook which was flowing through the midst of the land,
the kings of the Assyrians might arrive and find an abundance of water.”
he built up the entire wall that had been broken apart.
And he constructed towers upon it,
And he made all kinds of weapons and shields.
And he appointed leaders of the warriors within the army.
et convocavit universos in platea portæ civitatis,
And he summoned them all to the wide street of the gate of the city.
ac locutus est ad cor eorum,
And he spoke to their heart,
nec paveatis regem Assyriorum, et universam multitudinem quæ est cum eo:
Neither should you dread the king of the Assyrians and the entire multitude that is with him.
multo enim plures nobiscum sunt, quam cum illo.
For many more are with us than with him.
Cum illo enim est brachium carneum:
For with him is an arm of flesh;
with us is the Lord our God,
Confortatusque est populus hujuscemodi verbis Ezechiæ regis Juda.
And the people were strengthened by this type of words from Hezekiah, the king of Judah.
misit Sennacherib rex Assyriorum servos suos in Jerusalem (ipse enim cum universo exercitu obsidebat Lachis) ad Ezechiam regem Juda,
the king of the Assyrians, sent his servants to Jerusalem, (for he and his entire army were besieging Lachish) to Hezekiah,
et ad omnem populum qui erat in urbe,
the king of Judah, and to all the people who were in the city,
“Thus says Sennacherib, the king of the Assyrians:
In quo habentes fiduciam sedetis obsessi in Jerusalem?
In whom do you have faith, as you sit besieged in Jerusalem?
ut tradat morti in fame et siti,
so that he would deliver you to die from hunger and thirst,
affirmans quod Dominus Deus vester liberet vos de manu regis Assyriorum?
by affirming that the Lord your God will free you from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?
Is this not the same Hezekiah who destroyed his own high places
and you shall burn incense upon it?’
an ignoratis quæ ego fecerim, et patres mei, cunctis terrarum populis?
Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands?
numquid prævaluerunt dii gentium, omniumque terrarum, liberare regionem suam de manu mea?
Have the gods of the nations and all the lands prevailed so as to free their region from my hand?
Quis est de universis diis gentium,
out of all the gods of the nations that my fathers destroyed,
qui potuerit eruere populum suum de manu mea,
who is able to rescue his people from my hand,
ut possit etiam Deus vester eruere vos de hac manu?
so that now also your God would be able to rescue you from this hand?
let not Hezekiah deceive or delude you with vain persuasion.
And you should not believe him.
Si enim nullus potuit deus cunctarum gentium atque regnorum liberare populum suum de manu mea,
For if no god out of all the nations and kingdoms was able to free his people from my hand,
and from the hand of my fathers,
consequenter nec Deus vester poterit eruere vos de manu mea.
consequently neither will your God be able to rescue you from my hand.”
et alia multa locuti sunt servi ejus contra Dominum Deum,
his servants were speaking many other things against the Lord God,
Epistolas quoque scripsit plenas blasphemiæ in Dominum Deum Israël,
he wrote letters full of blasphemy against the Lord God of Israel.
Sicut dii gentium ceterarum non potuerunt liberare populum suum de manu mea,
“Just as the gods of other nations were unable to free their people from my hand,
et Deus Ezechiæ eruere non poterit populum suum de manu ista.
so also is the God of Hezekiah unable to rescue his people from this hand.”
he also shouted with a great clamor,
contra populum qui sedebat in muris Jerusalem,
in the language of the Jews,
toward the people who were sitting upon the walls of Jerusalem,
so that he might frighten them
And he was speaking against the God of Jerusalem,
just as against the gods of the peoples of the earth,
which are works of the hands of men.
and Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz,
ac vociferati sunt usque in cælum.
and they cried out to heaven.
And the Lord sent an Angel,
who struck all the experienced men
and the leaders of the army of the king of the Assyrians.
reversusque est cum ignominia in terram suam.
And he returned in disgrace to his own land.
Cumque ingressus esset domum dei sui,
And when he had entered the house of his god,
filii qui egressi fuerant de utero ejus interfecerunt eum gladio.
the sons who had gone forth from his loins killed him with the sword.
And the Lord saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib,
et habitatores Jerusalem de manu Sennacherib regis Assyriorum,
and from the hand of all.
et præstitit eis quietem per circuitum.
And he presented to them peace on every side.
Multi etiam deferebant hostias et sacrificia Domino in Jerusalem,
And now many were bringing victims and sacrifices to the Lord in Jerusalem,
and gifts to Hezekiah, the king of Judah.
qui exaltatus est post hæc coram cunctis gentibus.
And after these things, he was exalted before all the nations.
In diebus illis ægrotavit Ezechias usque ad mortem,
In those days, Hezekiah was sick, even unto death,
and he prayed to the Lord.
and gave to him a sign.
Sed non juxta beneficia quæ acceperat,
But he did not repay according to the benefits which he had received,
for his heart was lifted up.
And so wrath was brought against him,
et facta est contra eum ira,
And after this, he was humbled,
eo quod exaltatum fuisset cor ejus,
because he had exalted his heart,
both he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
et idcirco non venit super eos ira Domini in diebus Ezechiæ.
And therefore the wrath of the Lord did not overwhelm them in the days of Hezekiah.
et thesauros sibi plurimos congregavit argenti,
And he gathered for himself many treasures of silver
and stalls for every beast of burden,
And he built for himself cities.
he had innumerable herds and flocks of sheep.
eo quod dedisset ei Dominus substantiam multam nimis.
For the Lord had given to him an exceedingly great substance.
This same Hezekiah was the one who blocked the upper font of the waters of Gihon,
qui obturavit superiorem fontem aquarum Gihon,
and who diverted them down to the western part of the City of David.
et avertit eas subter ad occidentem urbis David:
in omnibus operibus suis fecit prospere quæ voluit.
he prosperously accomplished whatever he willed.
Yet still, concerning the legates from the leaders of Babylon,
qui missi fuerant ad eum ut interrogarent de portento quod acciderat super terram,
who had been sent to him so that they might inquire about the portent which had happened upon the earth,
God permitted him to be tempted,
et nota fierent omnia quæ erant in corde ejus.
so that everything might be made known which was in his heart.
Now the rest of the words of Hezekiah,
scripta sunt in visione Isaiæ filii Amos prophetæ,
have been written in the vision of the prophet Isaiah,
and in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
And Hezekiah slept with his fathers.
et sepelierunt eum super sepulchra filiorum David:
And they buried him above the sepulchers of the sons of David.
et celebravit ejus exequias universus Juda,
And all of Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem,
celebrated his funeral. And his son,
regnavitque Manasses filius ejus pro eo.
